components.text: Recent official research reports consistently show that Bengaluru floods when heavy rainfall meets drainage system has lost capacity [16]. The city’s average annual rainfall was reported at 969 mm during 203–9, and recent studies note that intense rainfall events can overwhelm drains, especially where runoff has increased because of urbanization [2].

Rainfall is the trigger, but not the sole cause. The ATREE action plan notes that higher rainfall intensity and changing rainfall patterns worsen flooding, while the Comptroller and Auditor General report says storm-water planning did not adequately account for high-intensity rainfall rainfall under rapid urban growth.

Drainage failure is a central factor. The CAG report found large-scale encroachment of lakes and drains, poor maintenance missing drain drain inventories and sewage mixing with stormwater; it also said many drains lacked boundary markings, enabled encroachment and blockage . Research on Bengaluru similarly states that natural channels have been narrowed or blocked and artificial drains are often blocked [188][].

Construction contributes in two ways: it increases impervious surfaces, and it physically obstructs natural drainsplains. ATREE reports a rise in impervious and loss of blue-green cover, while IIS-linked studies-valley high-alteration of topography reduce infiltration and runoff [1212]

Solid waste is a direct operational because litter, debris, and garbage choke drains. IISc and ATREE sources explicitly identify litter, building debris and municipal waste major causes of blockage, and the CAG report notes that sewage and waste in drains worsen flooding and water pollution [3]
Keep drains courtyard drains roadside inlets clear; Avoid dumping waste into streets; Elevate critical appliances and documents above flood levels; Use rainwater harvesting feasible.
These actions reduce local damage but cannot fix upstream drainage failures or lake encroachment.
